 Cupid Limited reported a 132 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated total income to Rs 208.97 crore in Q2 FY27 , while net profit rose 133 per cent to Rs 56.22 crore. Operating income increased 122 per cent to Rs 187.86 crore, and EBITDA stood at Rs 54.77 crore, with a margin of 29 per cent. Profit before tax grew 126 per cent to Rs 72.89 crore. For the first half of FY27, total income rose 136 per cent to Rs 365.95 crore, while operating income increased 137 per cent to Rs 342.58 crore. EBITDA grew 156 per cent to Rs 114.83 crore and net profit increased 156 per cent to Rs 100.37 crore. Domestic business contributed Rs 224.64 crore, accounting for 67 per cent of H1 sales, compared with 41 per cent in FY26. The Consumer Healthcare and FMCG business contributed Rs 166.88 crore, or 49 per cent of sales, while international business generated Rs 112.73 crore. The company expects its domestic consumer business to gain from two organised retail partnerships. Its products are set to reach more than 290 Style Baazar stores, with an expected contribution of around Rs 200 crore in FY27. Under a separate partnership with V2 Retail, Cupid will have dedicated space of around 400 sq ft across more than 425 stores. Supplies began in November, with availability across the network targeted by mid-December. The company expects the V2 partnership to generate at least Rs 400 crore in revenue over the next 12 months. Cupid's new manufacturing facility at Palava, Maharashtra, is scheduled for commissioning in Q3 FY27. At full capacity, the facility is expected to increase annual production capacity to around 1.25 billion male condoms and 125 million female condoms, from 480 million and 52 million, respectively, at its existing Sinnar facility. The company said the facility's dual-polymer production lines would support both natural rubber latex and nitrile products. Cupid has raised its FY27 guidance to revenue of at least Rs 880 crore and net profit of Rs 275 crore or more. It has also set FY28 revenue guidance at Rs 1,305 crore or more and net profit of around Rs 390 crore, followed by FY29 revenue of at least Rs 1,950 crore and net profit of around Rs 605 crore. The company said it expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1, supported by the Palava facility, festive demand and the ramp-up of organised retail partnerships. The company is also exploring a manufacturing venture with a South African partner, in which it may hold up to 49 per cent, and evaluating a medical-devices manufacturing project in West Bengal. In July 2026, it made a follow-on investment of $5 million in GII Healthcare Investment Limited. Chairman and managing director Aditya Kumar Halwasiya said the company would continue expanding its domestic consumer business and international healthcare operations, adding that it aims to become debt-free over time.
